en.title: Thomasin McKenzie Faces New Fallout Frontier in Season 3
en.summary: Fresh off acclaimed roles, Thomasin McKenzie is set to bring her talents to the post-apocalyptic world of Prime Video's Fallout. The acclaimed actress will face a significant new challenge as she joins the recurring cast for the upcoming third season.
en.body:
The Wasteland is expanding, and **Thomasin McKenzie** is stepping into its irradiated landscape. Known for her nuanced performances in independent cinema, including **"Eileen"** and **"Jojo Rabbit,"** McKenzie has officially joined the recurring cast of Prime Video's hit series **"Fallout"** for its highly anticipated Season 3. This marks a significant venture for the New Zealand-born actress into the realm of large-scale genre television, promising a fresh dynamic for fans of the post-apocalyptic saga.

Mckenzie's presence in **"Fallout"** Season 3 is particularly intriguing given the show's ambitious production methods. The series, adapted from Bethesda's beloved video game franchise, is celebrated for its immersive world-building, seamlessly blending practical effects with advanced visual technology, including the use of Volume. This innovative filming technique, which creates vast, dynamic sets within a virtual environment, is something McKenzie notes as a departure from her previous work. "My previous roles never required technology like this," she has shared, highlighting that **"Fallout"** presents a unique acting challenge that she's eager to embrace as production kicks off in Los Angeles.

## A New Horizon for a Rising Star

**Thomasin McKenzie's** ascent in Hollywood has been meteoric. After early roles, including a brief appearance in **Peter Jackson's "The Hobbit"** trilogy, she captured critical attention with performances in **M. Night Shyamalan's "Old,"** **Jane Campion's "The Power of the Dog,"** and Edgar Wright's **"Last Night in Soho."** Her recent work alongside Anya Taylor-Joy in **"Last Night in Soho"** and her upcoming gothic horror film **"Victorian Psycho"** with Maika Monroe further cement her status as a versatile talent. Joining **"Fallout"** alongside fellow new recurring cast members **Manny Jacinto** and **Emily Mortimer**, and returning stars like Ella Purnell and Aaron Paul, positions McKenzie at the heart of one of streaming's most talked-about series.

## What This Means for the Fallout Fandom

The addition of **Thomasin McKenzie** to the **"Fallout"** universe is already generating considerable buzz among the dedicated fanbase. Her reputation for delivering emotionally resonant and complex characters suggests she will bring a compelling depth to her role within the established lore of the **"Fallout"** games and the series' narrative. Fans are speculating about which faction or survivor she might portray, given her proven ability to embody characters navigating difficult and often morally ambiguous circumstances. The series' commitment to authentic world-building, from the irradiated landscapes to the iconic Vault-Tec bunkers, provides fertile ground for an actress of McKenzie's caliber to explore new dramatic territories.

## What's Next

Filming for **"Fallout"** Season 3 is currently underway in Los Angeles. While specific details about McKenzie's character and the plot of the new season have not yet been announced, the production's return to its Los Angeles base suggests a deepening exploration of the iconic Californian wasteland setting. Fans can anticipate more updates as production progresses throughout the year.

content_raw: After a handful of small roles, including a walk-on part in Peter Jackson ’s The Hobbit trilogy, New Zealand actress Thomasin McKenzie earned her place on the roster in several independent films. Just as we were entering the 2020s, McKenzie’s career soared with roles in M. Night Shyamalan ’s Old , Jane Campion ’s The Power of the Dog , and the top of the call sheet, opposite Anya Taylor-Joy , in Edgar Wright ’s Last Night in Soho . We’ll next spot her sharing scenes with genre queen Maika Monroe in their Gothic horror, Victorian Psycho , hitting theaters this weekend.
